subject: chemistry
title: Cathode-ray evidence: charge versus straight-line travel
official_title: Demonstrating the properties of cathode rays

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Interpret a fictional teacher-provided recording; no apparatus construction or electrical operation is requested.
tasks: Name the particles in the beam.
Infer their charge from the electric-field observation.
Identify the evidence for straight-line travel.
State one property consistent with paddle-wheel motion.
Predict deflection if the plate polarities are exchanged.
marks: Negative: attraction towards the positive plate.
The sharp shadow of the cross.
Transfer of momentum/energy to the wheel is consistent with particle behaviour.
Deflection reverses towards the newly positive plate.
worked_explanation: The field supplies a force on charged particles; the direction reveals the negative sign. The shadow supports straight-line travel in the field-free region. Wheel motion is supporting evidence of transfer, not a quantitative measurement of electron mass.
common_error: Calling motion towards the positive plate evidence of positive charge.
transfer_question: A beam shows no deflection in a field-free region. Does that establish that the particles are neutral?
transfer_answer: No. A charged beam can travel straight when no transverse force acts.

subject: chemistry
title: Distinguish molecular shape from electron-domain geometry
official_title: Displaying the shapes of molecules and ions using models

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Use VSEPR on four labelled model cards. A multiple bond counts as one domain.
tasks: Give the electron-domain geometry of NH3.
worked_explanation: CH4, NH3 and H2O each have four electron domains, but shape names describe atom positions rather than lone pairs. Carbonate has three bonding domains in a plane; its resonance description does not require three different permanent C-O bond lengths.
common_error: Counting the C=O drawing as two separate VSEPR domains.
transfer_question: A model has six domains, four bonding and two opposite lone pairs (XeF4). What is its molecular shape?
transfer_answer: Square planar.

subject: chemistry
title: Burette difference and balance zero correction
official_title: Handling glassware and four beam balance

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Read supplied instrument records. Assume the balance zero error stayed unchanged between both weighings.
tasks: Select a volumetric flask or beaker for defining an accurate final solution volume.
Explain why the constant zero error cancels in the mass difference.
marks: The same +0.02 g is subtracted from both readings, so their difference is unchanged.
worked_explanation: Sample mass = 14.98-12.36. Absolute readings need the zero correction, while equal additive offsets cancel in differences. A burette measures volume delivered from final minus initial reading.
common_error: Adding the zero correction to a reading that is already too high.
transfer_question: If the balance zero changed by +0.03 g between empty and loaded readings, would cancellation still be valid?
transfer_answer: No. A changed offset biases the mass difference by 0.03 g.

subject: chemistry
title: Anhydrous carbonate standard: mass and dilution audit
official_title: Preparation of standard solutions

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Audit concentration calculations from a completed fictional preparation record. No chemical preparation is requested.
tasks: Convert the stock volume to dm3.
Calculate moles in the 20.00 cm3 aliquot.
worked_explanation: n=m/M=1.325/106.0; c=n/0.2500. Dilution conserves the aliquot solute amount: 0.05000 x 0.02000 mol remains in 0.1000 dm3.
common_error: Dividing by the volume of water added rather than final solution volume.
transfer_question: What mass of the same anhydrous solute corresponds to 100.0 cm3 of 0.02000 mol dm-3 solution?

subject: chemistry
title: Oxygen molar volume from mass-loss and dry-gas data
official_title: Experimental determination of molar volume of a gas.

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: Corrected dry O2 volume at stated laboratory T,p
scenario: The gas-producing reaction has O2 as its only escaping product; volume is already corrected for water vapour and pressure. Use only the supplied analytical records.
tasks: Calculate molar volume at these conditions.
Predict how a leak, with unchanged measured mass loss, biases this result.
marks: Some O2 escapes measurement, so measured volume and molar volume are too low.
worked_explanation: Mass loss gives oxygen amount without treating the whole solid as oxygen. Vm=V/n=0.0960/(0.128/32.0). The result applies to the stated laboratory conditions, not every T and p.
common_error: Using 22.4 dm3 mol-1 automatically despite different stated gas conditions.
transfer_question: At the same T,p a second record loses 0.160 g O2. What dry volume follows from Vm=24.0 dm3 mol-1?

subject: chemistry
title: Magnesium molar mass with water-vapour correction
official_title: Experimental determination of molar mass of magnesium using molar volume of hydrogen gas

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Use Mg + 2H+ -> Mg2+ + H2. Liquid levels are equal, and Mg is assumed pure and fully reacted. Report three significant figures.
tasks: State the direction of error if water-vapour pressure is not subtracted.
marks: H2 amount is overestimated, so calculated Mg molar mass is too low.
worked_explanation: p(H2)=101.0-3.0. n(H2)=pV/RT=98.0 x 0.0504/(8.314 x 298). The 1:1 equation makes n(Mg)=n(H2); M(Mg)=mass/amount.
common_error: Reporting molar mass with units as if it were the dimensionless relative atomic mass.
transfer_question: If 5% of the hydrogen leaks away while the Mg mass remains correct, how does calculated molar mass change?
transfer_answer: It becomes too high, by factor 1/0.95 (about 5.26%).

subject: chemistry
title: Neutralisation calorimetry: sign and mole basis
official_title: Experimental determination of the enthalpy of acid/base neutralization (NaOH and HCl, KOH and HNO3, NaOH and CH3COOH, NH4OH and HCl)

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: Strong acid and strong base amounts
scenario: Assume complete H+ + OH- -> H2O, negligible calorimeter heat capacity and no heat loss.
tasks: Give heat released by reaction including sign.
worked_explanation: The warming solution gains positive mcΔT. Under the assumptions, reaction heat is its negative. Divide reaction heat in kJ by the 0.0500 mol of water formed.
common_error: A positive temperature change does not mean a positive reaction enthalpy.
transfer_question: The same reaction is measured in a cup with heat capacity 20.0 J K-1. How much extra heat is accounted for at ΔT=6.7 K?
transfer_answer: 134 J; add it to solution heat before changing the sign for reaction heat.

subject: chemistry
title: Hess cycle: dissolve then neutralise
official_title: Validation of Hess Law through experiment

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: Path at matched final solution state
Direct NaOH(s)+HCl(aq) to same final state
scenario: All values refer to one mole of NaOH, the same temperature and matched concentrations/final solvent amount. Differences are experimental.
tasks: Calculate the absolute discrepancy between paths.
Give the sign if the dissolution step is reversed.
marks: Enthalpy is a state function; matched initial and final states have the same ΔH.
worked_explanation: Adding dissolution and aqueous neutralisation cancels aqueous NaOH. The measured discrepancy does not refute Hess law; non-identical final dilution states or heat losses can cause it.
common_error: Adding calorimetry values from different final dilution states without a correction.
transfer_question: If dissolution is -44.0 and direct reaction -101.0 kJ mol-1 at matched states, infer aqueous neutralisation ΔH.

subject: chemistry
title: Interpret sodium and magnesium observation cards
official_title: Comparison of reactions of s block metals with air, water and acids

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: These are fictional observation summaries, not directions for carrying out reactions.
tasks: Which metal reacts more visibly with cold water?
Name the gas expected for sodium-water reaction.
Name the principal soluble alkaline product of sodium-water reaction.
Explain why air-exposed magnesium may react slowly at first.
marks: A surface oxide layer can impede contact/reaction.
worked_explanation: The alkaline solution and hydrogen are consistent with 2Na+2H2O->2NaOH+H2. Magnesium behaviour also depends on protective films; rates are not determined by position alone.
common_error: Interpreting a slow visible change as proof of no possible reaction.
transfer_question: A cleaned Mg sample reacts faster initially than an oxide-coated one in otherwise matched acid data. Does this alone prove a different intrinsic rate constant?
transfer_answer: No. Surface condition/contact has changed; the comparison does not isolate the intrinsic rate constant.

subject: chemistry
title: Flame-colour identification with a contamination control
official_title: Identifi cation of elements in compounds by the fl ame test (Li, Na, K, Ca, Sr, Ba)

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Candidates are sodium, potassium and barium salts, one per coded sample. Interpret supplied colour records only.
tasks: Explain why the initial blank matters.
State the electronic origin of emitted light.
marks: Yellow contamination could falsely suggest sodium in an unknown.
Excited electrons return to lower energy levels and emit characteristic photon energies.
worked_explanation: The candidate list and blank make colour assignments defensible. Cobalt glass can help reveal potassium emission when sodium yellow dominates; it does not prove sample purity.
common_error: Naming the anion from a flame colour that mainly indicates the metal.
transfer_question: Two known sodium salts with different anions both show yellow flames. Which component is supported as the source of the characteristic colour?
transfer_answer: The common sodium component, not the different anions.

subject: chemistry
title: Separate sulfate, sulfite and thiosulfate evidence
official_title: Identifi cation of anions (SO4 2-, SO3 2-, S2O3 2-, S2-, CO3 2-, NO3 -, NO2 -,)

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: White barium precipitate persists in dilute acid
White barium precipitate disappears in dilute acid; gas reduces dichromate indicator
Acidified sample becomes cloudy with sulfur; evolved gas reduces dichromate indicator
scenario: Each sample contains one of SO4^2-, SO3^2- or S2O3^2-. No tests are to be performed.
tasks: Write the net acid reaction of Q.
Write the net acid reaction of R.
worked_explanation: Sulfate gives acid-resistant BaSO4. Sulfite yields SO2 but no elemental sulfur in this pattern. Thiosulfate gives both SO2 and sulfur, so the cloudy sulfur observation distinguishes it.
common_error: Using gas reduction alone to distinguish sulfite from thiosulfate.
transfer_question: A fourth sample effervesces with acid and its gas gives a white limewater precipitate; no sulfur cloudiness occurs. Name the likely anion and balanced acid equation.
transfer_answer: Carbonate: CO3^2- + 2H+ -> CO2 + H2O.

subject: chemistry
title: Nitrogen-in-air evidence from a nitride record
official_title: Showing the presence of nitrogen in air by experiment

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: Contains oxide and a nitride candidate
Gas turns damp red litmus blue
scenario: Analyse the handbook nitride-to-ammonia route, rather than estimating nitrogen percentage from an air-volume remainder.
tasks: Name the nitride consistent with the magnesium residue.
Balance nitride formation from Mg and N2.
Explain the value of the MgO control.
marks: Oxide alone does not account for the nitrogen-containing gas response.
worked_explanation: Nitride contains nitrogen from air; hydrolysis produces ammonia. The qualitative chain supports nitrogen presence, but does not measure its proportion in air or establish a pure nitride residue.
common_error: Claiming that this qualitative activity measures air as exactly 78% nitrogen.
transfer_question: A theoretical 0.0020 mol Mg3N2 hydrolyses completely. Calculate the NH3 amount.
transfer_answer: 0.0040 mol because nitride:ammonia is 1:2.

subject: chemistry
title: Halide identification using colour and ammonia behaviour
official_title: Identifi cation of halides

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: Persists in dilute, dissolves in concentrated ammonia
scenario: The only candidates are separate chloride, bromide and iodide solutions. Interpret the pre-recorded matrix.
tasks: Explain why ammonia behaviour strengthens colour evidence.
marks: It adds a second distinguishing observation; similar-looking colours alone can be misread.
worked_explanation: AgCl, AgBr and AgI give the white, cream and yellow patterns respectively. The different ammonia solubilities help distinguish the separate samples; mixed samples need more cautious interpretation.
common_error: Saying all silver halides dissolve in dilute ammonia.
transfer_question: Can a yellow precipitate alone establish that a mixed sample contains only iodide?
transfer_answer: No. It supports iodide in the given context but cannot exclude other components.

subject: chemistry
title: Iodate-to-thiosulfate mole-chain audit
official_title: Standardization of a solution of thiosulphate ions using KIO3 and KI

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: 1 IO3- produces 3 I2; 1 I2 consumes 2 S2O3^2-
scenario: Use fictional titration data with excess iodide and sufficient acid assumed; no reagent preparation is requested.
worked_explanation: The stoichiometric chain is 1:3:6 for iodate:iodine:thiosulfate. Hence c(thiosulfate)=6 x 0.01000 x 0.02000/0.02400.
common_error: Using 1:1 iodate:thiosulfate rather than the combined 1:6 ratio.
transfer_question: If the iodate aliquot halves with the same thiosulfate concentration, what mean titre is expected?

subject: chemistry
title: Ammonium ion versus ammonia gas
official_title: Identifi cation of ammonia gas and ammonium salts

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: Recorded gas evidence after alkaline treatment
Moist red litmus blue; white fumes with HCl record
scenario: Candidates are NH4Cl(aq), NH3(aq) and NaCl(aq). Use the supplied records only.
tasks: Write the NH4+ and OH- net equation.
worked_explanation: NH4+ can donate a proton and acidifies its solution, whereas dissolved NH3 is basic. Both can provide ammonia gas under the appropriate recorded conditions; the original solution behaviour distinguishes them.
common_error: Calling NH4+ itself a gas or assuming ammonium chloride solution is alkaline.
transfer_question: Why must litmus be moist for an ammonia gas indication?
transfer_answer: Water permits ammonia dissolution and acid-base action that produces OH- and changes the indicator.

subject: chemistry
title: Use a salt-solubility matrix without overgeneralising
official_title: Testing the solubility of salts of s block elements

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: All records are fictional, at the same temperature and specified comparable analytical conditions. Clear means no visible precipitate, not proof of infinite solubility.
tasks: Identify a sulfate precipitate formula supported by the table.
Write the barium carbonate precipitation equation.
State the contrasting qualitative Group2 sulfate and hydroxide solubility trends supported.
Explain why a clear solution is limited evidence.
marks: Sulfate solubility generally decreases and hydroxide solubility generally increases down Group2.
Concentrations may be below precipitation threshold; a sparingly soluble salt need not visibly precipitate.
worked_explanation: K+ remains soluble in these records. For Mg and Ba, the sulfate and hydroxide columns show opposite trends. Precipitation depends on ion product as well as Ksp.
common_error: Treating no visible precipitate as proof that every amount of the salt dissolves.
transfer_question: At fixed temperature an ion product is below Ksp. Is precipitation thermodynamically required?
transfer_answer: No; the solution is unsaturated with respect to that solid under the concentration approximation.

subject: chemistry
title: Thermal decomposition: carbonate versus nitrate products
official_title: Testing the thermal stability of nitrates and carbonates bicarbonates of s block elements

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: No measurable decomposition under the comparison conditions
MgO; brown gas and oxygen indications
scenario: Interpret records and reaction equations only; no heating operations are requested.
tasks: Explain greater thermal stability of Group2 carbonates down the group.
marks: Larger cations have lower polarising power, so distort carbonate less strongly.
worked_explanation: Do not use one universal product rule for all nitrates. Alkali nitrates such as KNO3 and Group2 nitrates such as Mg(NO3)2 have distinct product patterns.
common_error: Predicting that every nitrate yields only nitrite plus oxygen.
transfer_question: What amount of CO2 follows from complete decomposition of 0.010 mol NaHCO3?

subject: chemistry
title: Aqueous ion colours and electron configurations
official_title: Identifi cation of the colours of complex ions in aqueous medium

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Use four supplied aquated-ion reference records. Do not infer that every coloured ion has the same origin of colour.
tasks: Name the blue ion in this reference set.
Give the ligand in the aquated complexes.
Explain why Zn2+ lacks ordinary d-d colour in this comparison.
marks: The filled d subshell does not provide the partially filled split-d transition pattern responsible for these d-d colours.
worked_explanation: Copper(II), nickel(II) and cobalt(II) water-ligand complexes absorb selected visible wavelengths. The colour observed is transmitted light. Zinc(II) is d10, so the ordinary d-d explanation does not apply.
common_error: Claiming the observed blue is the wavelength most strongly absorbed.
transfer_question: Sc3+ is d0. Predict whether ordinary d-d transitions account for a visible colour.
transfer_answer: No: there are no d electrons for such transitions; its simple aquated ion is colourless.

subject: chemistry
title: Ferrous analysis with a concordant-titre decision
official_title: Determination of the concentration of a ferrous ion solution using acidifi ed potassium permanganate

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: Use the three careful titres; report mean to 0.01 cm3
scenario: The sample is sufficiently acidified. Use MnO4- + 8H+ + 5Fe2+ -> Mn2+ + 4H2O + 5Fe3+.
tasks: Calculate permanganate amount using the unrounded mean.
marks: First faint permanent pink/pale permanganate colour under the specified endpoint convention.
worked_explanation: The rough value is excluded under the declared rule. The 1:5 oxidant:iron ratio makes c(Fe2+)=5 c(MnO4-) V(MnO4-)/V(Fe2+). Keep the unrounded mean during calculation.
common_error: Averaging the rough result into an otherwise concordant set without a stated reason.
transfer_question: If air oxidises some Fe2+ before analysis, is the remaining Fe2+ titre higher or lower?
transfer_answer: Lower; less Fe2+ remains to consume permanganate.

subject: chemistry
title: Permanganate standardisation: repair the 2:5 equation
official_title: Determination of the concentration of KMnO4 solution using standard acidifi ed K2C2O4 solution.

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Use the supplied completed analytical records. Balance the half equations; do not copy a missing coefficient from a printed equation.
worked_explanation: Multiplying the manganese half equation by2 and oxalate half equation by5 gives equal electrons. Thus n(MnO4-)=2/5 n(oxalate), then divide by0.01980 dm3.
common_error: Using a 1:5 MnO4-:oxalate ratio from the handbook equation with its missing coefficient.
transfer_question: If 0.000300 mol MnO4- reacts, how much CO2 is produced?
transfer_answer: 0.00150 mol: each2 MnO4- corresponds to10 CO2.

subject: chemistry
title: Ligand change versus oxidation-state change
official_title: Observing the colours of Cu(II), Ni(II) and Co(II) salts with hydrochloric acid and ammonia solution

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Use teacher-supplied ligand-equilibrium observations; avoid treating mixed colours as pure-species spectra.
tasks: Write the formula of the deep-blue copper ammonia complex commonly represented in this syllabus.
Give Cu oxidation state before and after that ligand substitution.
Name the blue cobalt chloride complex.
Explain why changing ligand can change colour.
marks: Ligands change the energies of the split d orbitals and hence visible absorption.
worked_explanation: Cu and Co remain +2 in the stated substitution examples. Ligand exchange changes the coordination environment; it need not be redox. The copper chloride-rich yellow-green appearance can reflect overlapping species.
common_error: Inferring oxidation from every colour change.
transfer_question: Does replacing neutral H2O by neutral NH3 necessarily change the charge of a Cu(II) complex?
transfer_answer: No. Neutral ligand substitution leaves the formal complex charge unchanged if ligand numbers and other charges are as stated.

subject: chemistry
title: Manganese oxidation states from labelled species
official_title: Experimental observations of different oxidation states (+2,+4,+6,+7) of manganese containing compounds using \ redox reactions

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: These are independently supplied species records, not a sequence to reproduce. Determine redox changes algebraically.
tasks: Give Mn oxidation state in MnO4-.
Give Mn oxidation state in MnO4^2-.
Give Mn oxidation state in MnO2.
Give electrons gained per Mn for MnO4- to Mn2+.
Balance the acidic MnO4- to Mn2+ reduction half equation.
worked_explanation: With oxygen assigned -2, the oxygen total is -8 in each tetraoxo species; their different ion charges give +7 and+6 for Mn. Purple-to-nearly-colourless may accompany reduction to+2 in acidic analysis, but colour alone requires context.
common_error: Assigning manganese oxidation state from ion charge without including oxygen.
transfer_question: How many electrons per Mn are gained in MnO4- -> MnO2?
transfer_answer: 3, because +7 becomes +4.

subject: chemistry
title: Distinguish Cu2+, Fe3+ and Cr3+ using paired records
official_title: Tests to identify Ni2+, Fe2+, Fe3+, Cu2+ and Cr3+ ions using NaOH and NH3

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: Dissolves in excess NH3 to deep blue
Persists in excess NaOH; thiocyanate gives blood-red solution
scenario: Only Cu2+, Fe3+ and Cr3+ are possible, one in each sample. Interpret observations without carrying out tests.
tasks: Write hydroxide precipitation equation for V.
Name the property illustrated by W with excess OH-.
marks: Amphoteric hydroxide behaviour; soluble hydroxo complex formation.
worked_explanation: Blue hydroxide with deep-blue ammonia complex supports Cu2+. Red-brown hydroxide and blood-red thiocyanate evidence support Fe3+. Chromium(III) hydroxide can dissolve in excess hydroxide; precipitate colour alone is insufficient.
common_error: Treating Fe2+ green hydroxide and Fe3+ brown hydroxide as interchangeable.
transfer_question: A fourth sample initially gives green Fe(OH)2 which becomes brown in air. What process explains the change?
transfer_answer: Oxidation of iron(II) to iron(III), producing iron(III) hydroxide.

subject: chemistry
title: Unsaturation evidence does not uniquely identify an alkyne
official_title: Observation of reactions and properties of Alkene and Alkyne.

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: No change under stated dark conditions
scenario: Candidates are ethene, ethyne and ethane. The acetylide evidence is already supplied; no preparation or isolation of sensitive compounds is requested.
tasks: Assign X within the given candidates.
Assign Y within the given candidates.
Assign Z within the given candidates.
State why bromine-water evidence alone cannot separate X and Y.
Write the one-equivalent addition equation for ethene and Br2.
marks: Both contain carbon-carbon multiple bonds and can undergo addition.
worked_explanation: Use the joint pattern. The terminal-alkyne record adds selectivity that the two unsaturation observations lack. A negative terminal-alkyne record alone would not exclude an internal alkyne in a broader candidate list.
common_error: Calling every bromine-decolourising hydrocarbon an alkene.
transfer_question: An internal alkyne gives negative terminal-alkyne evidence. Can it still decolourise bromine?
transfer_answer: Yes; it retains a C≡C bond despite having no terminal alkyne hydrogen.

subject: chemistry
title: Alcohol oxidation records: ethanol versus propan-2-ol
official_title: Examination of the properties of alcohols.

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results. Index/catalogue says p.80; actual activity begins on printed p.78 (PDF86).

data: Methanoic acid in stated partial oxidation record
scenario: Interpret given product-identification records. These are not instructions for oxidation. Handbook activity actually starts on printed p.78.
tasks: Give the functional group of propanone.
Explain why orange-to-green alone does not distinguish these alcohols.
marks: All three show oxidation under the stated records; product evidence is needed.
worked_explanation: Ethanol has the OH-bearing carbon attached to one other carbon; propan-2-ol has it attached to two. Oxidant colour loss is common evidence, while the carbonyl/acid product differentiates alcohol class.
common_error: Assuming every positive alcohol oxidation produces a carboxylic acid.
transfer_question: What is the usual oxidation product class of a secondary alcohol without carbon-skeleton cleavage?
transfer_answer: A ketone.

subject: chemistry
title: Phenol: paired evidence for acidity and substitution
official_title: Examination of the properties of phenol.

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: No analogous salt formation with aqueous NaOH
scenario: Use the supplied comparison; interpretation is restricted to these candidates and conditions.
tasks: Identify the reference producing the violet colour.
Name the white precipitate from phenol in this record.
Explain why phenol is more acidic than ethanol.
marks: Phenoxide is stabilised by delocalisation of negative charge into the aromatic system.
worked_explanation: The OH group is directly attached to the aromatic ring in phenol. Its conjugate base and ring reactivity differ from ethanol. Bromine decolourisation in this case is aromatic substitution, not proof of an alkene group.
common_error: Explaining phenol bromination as alkene addition.
transfer_question: Why can bromine decolourisation by itself not distinguish phenol from an alkene?
transfer_answer: Both can consume bromine by different reaction types; additional evidence such as the characteristic phenol precipitate/FeCl3 pattern is needed.

subject: chemistry
title: Carbonyl identification with the aromatic-aldehyde exception
official_title: Tests for aldehydes and ketones.

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Only ethanal, benzaldehyde and propanone are candidates. These are archived observations, not reagent instructions.
tasks: State what all three positive DNP records support.
Explain why a negative Fehling record does not alone prove ketone.
marks: An aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group in this candidate set.
Benzaldehyde is an aldehyde but does not give the ordinary positive Fehling pattern.
worked_explanation: The broad carbonyl record groups the three candidates. Tollens differentiates the two aldehydes from propanone; Fehling distinguishes the aliphatic aldehyde from benzaldehyde in this set.
common_error: Equating Fehling-negative with ketone in every case.
transfer_question: A carbonyl compound gives DNP precipitate and Tollens silver mirror but is Fehling-negative. Is an aromatic aldehyde consistent?
transfer_answer: Yes; benzaldehyde is a consistent example within these syllabus candidates.

subject: chemistry
title: Carboxylic-acid evidence and the methanoic-acid exception
official_title: Examination of the properties of carboxylic acids.

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

scenario: Use the fictional comparison to distinguish acidity from reducing behaviour. No tasting or reagent handling is requested.
tasks: Name the gas in the carbonate records.
Write the net acid/carbonate equation using RCOOH.
Identify the reducing acid in this set.
Explain benzoic acid dissolving in aqueous NaOH.
marks: It forms soluble benzoate salt by deprotonation.
worked_explanation: All three carboxylic acids can neutralise carbonate. The Tollens-positive behaviour of methanoic acid is an important exception to treating all carboxylic acids as non-reducing in this context.
common_error: Calling a Tollens-positive methanoic acid sample an aldehyde without the acid evidence.
transfer_question: A benzoic-acid/neutral-ketone mixture gives a soluble benzoate fraction on acid-base conversion. Which component undergoes the acid-base change?
transfer_answer: Benzoic acid; the neutral ketone does not become a carboxylate.

subject: chemistry
title: Aniline and azo-linkage evidence: interpret supplied structures
official_title: Tests for aniline.

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: No persistent comparable aromatic diazonium intermediate
scenario: Interpret the handbook diazonium/azo-dye concept from completed records only. No quantities, temperatures, mixing steps or synthesis instructions are supplied.
tasks: Name the amine class of aniline.
Identify the azo linkage in the product fragment.
State the named reaction class linking the aromatic components.
Explain why the aliphatic comparison need not give the same persistent intermediate.
marks: Aliphatic diazonium ions are much less stable and readily lose nitrogen; the same persistent aromatic coupling route cannot be assumed.
worked_explanation: The molecular fragment and orange-red product are consistent with an azo dye derived from an aromatic diazonium species. Colour alone is not a unique structural identification; the supplied fragment is independent evidence.
common_error: Confusing the -N=N- azo linkage with a diazonium group in the intermediate.
transfer_question: Would an orange dye alone prove an azo linkage if no structural evidence were supplied?
transfer_answer: No. Many chromophores produce colours; a colour observation alone cannot establish -N=N-.

subject: chemistry
title: Magnesium rate comparison at a fixed gas endpoint
official_title: Experimental determination of the effect of acid concentration on the reaction rate between Mg and acid reaction

source_verification.note: Activity heading and relevant method/analysis inspected in official NIE PDF; exercise is original interpretation of fictional results.

data: Time to same 10.0 cm3 H2 endpoint / s
